title: Variational inference and the evidence lower bound

items.title: Variational family and evidence lower bound
items.statement: On a measure space (Ω,𝒜,μ), let γ≥0 be measurable with Z=∫γ dμ∈(0,∞), and define π=γ/Z. A probability density q is admissible when q=0 μ-a.e. on {π=0} and ∫q(|log γ|+|log q|)dμ<∞, with zero-density terms set to zero. Define ELBO(q)=∫q(log γ−log q)dμ. A variational family is a nonempty set of admissible q. On a finite product reference space, the mean-field family consists of admissible product densities q(z)=∏j qj(zj). Use log(0)=-infinity, define all four zero-density weighted log terms as zero, and extend weighted terms by zero on the measurable null set where gamma or q is infinite.

references.title: David M. Blei, Alp Kucukelbir, and Jon D. McAuliffe, Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians (2017)

Ronghuo Zheng, Zhiting Hu, and Yuntian Deng, 10-708 Probabilistic Graphical Models, Lecture 13: Variational Inference II (2015)

items.title: Evidence lower bound is log evidence minus reverse KL
items.statement: For every admissible q, let Q=qμ and Π=πμ. The density identity log Z=ELBO(q)+D(Q∥Π) holds under the library KL convention and AC. Since D(Q∥Π)≥0, ELBO(q)≤log Z. The identity is in the reverse-KL direction Q∥Π.

references.title: David M. Blei, Alp Kucukelbir, and Jon D. McAuliffe, Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians (2017)

items.title: Coordinate-ascent variational inference
items.statement: For a finite product reference space and an admissible initial mean-field density, perform a finite number of coordinate sweeps. For coordinate j, define hj(zj)=E_{q−j}logγ(zj,Z−j). Use qj*(zj)=exp(hj(zj))/cj only when the conditional expectation is well-defined and finite qj-a.e., cj=∫exp(hj)dμj is positive finite, and qj*q−j is admissible. Otherwise stop without that update. No convergence or global-optimality guarantee is part of the algorithm.

items.title: Gaussian mean-field reverse KL underestimates correlated marginal variance
items.statement: For a centered bivariate normal target with correlation ρ satisfying 0<|ρ|<1, maximization of the ELBO over independent Gaussian factors gives both factor variances 1−ρ², strictly below the target marginal variance 1.

references.title: David M. Blei, Alp Kucukelbir, and Jon D. McAuliffe, Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians (2017)

items.title: An admissible product has a finite coordinate normalizer
items.statement:
Use the admissible mean-field product $q=\prod_{k=1}^m q_k$ on the finite product of sigma-finite reference spaces in [[def-variational-family-and-elbo]]. Fix a coordinate $j$ and put $v=q_{-j}$, with the singleton unit-measure convention when $m=1$. Suppose
$$h_j(x)=\int v(y)\log\gamma(x,y)\,d\mu_{-j}(y)$$
has a measurable extended-real version defined without an $\infty-\infty$ ambiguity, finite for $q_j\mu_j$-almost every $x$. Products with a zero density are zero. Then $H:=\int v\log v\,d\mu_{-j}$ is a finite real number and
$$0<c_j:=\int e^{h_j(x)}\,d\mu_j(x)\le e^H Z<\infty.$$
This establishes normalization only; the resulting product must still satisfy the separate support and absolute-log-integrability conditions before it is an admissible coordinate replacement. No convergence or global-optimum conclusion is asserted.

items.title: Exact coordinate updates are monotone and finite sweeps have a call bound
items.statement: For a mean-field update satisfying the algorithm's finite conditional-expectation and positive finite normalizer conditions, if the resulting product density is admissible, then the displayed coordinate factor is an attained exact maximizer of ELBO over admissible replacements of that coordinate. Consequently each such update does not decrease ELBO. No convergence, stationary-point, or global-optimum conclusion follows.

references.title: David M. Blei, Alp Kucukelbir, and Jon D. McAuliffe, Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians (2017)
Michael I. Jordan, Zoubin Ghahramani, Tommi S. Jaakkola, and Lawrence K. Saul, An Introduction to Variational Methods for Graphical Models (1999)

items.title: A high ELBO alone does not certify posterior calibration
items.statement: The numerical value of an ELBO depends on the scale of the unnormalized target. It alone is not a bound on posterior discrepancy, calibration, or downstream error. Here a calibration guarantee means a separately proved property of repeated-sampling coverage or posterior-probability calibration; it is not defined by the ELBO. Under AC, the library KL identity controls the gap $\log Z-\operatorname{ELBO}(q)$ through the reverse divergence, when that gap is known.

references.title: David M. Blei, Alp Kucukelbir, and Jon D. McAuliffe, Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians (2017)

title: Variational inference and the evidence lower bound — Examples

items.title: Exact discrete variational family attains log evidence
items.statement: On a two-point counting space with γ(0)=2 and γ(1)=1, the posterior density is (2/3,1/3). Taking q equal to this posterior attains ELBO=log 3, while q=(1/2,1/2) gives a strictly smaller value.

items.title: A candidate outside posterior support is not admissible
items.statement: On a two-point counting space with γ=(1,0), the candidate density q=(0,1) violates q≪π and cannot have a finite ELBO.

items.title: Finite evidence and finite expected logs do not replace admissibility
items.statement: There are a finite-evidence target $\gamma$ and a supported product probability density $q$ for which $\int q|\log\gamma|d\mu<\infty$ and the expected-log coordinate function is identically zero on a countably infinite counting space, but its exponential has infinite normalizer. This $q$ fails the entropy-integrability part of admissibility; finite evidence and pointwise finite expected log alone do not justify a coordinate update.
